newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Stock clearance seen behind Hang Lung net.
newsitem.headline: Stock clearance seen behind Hang Lung net.

text.p: More profit from property sales helped Hang Lung Development Co Ltd and Amoy Properties Ltd lift their interim net profits above expectations, analysts said on Thursday.
But the full year still looks fairly dull with the group's property investment income flat and not much more sales income expected in the second half, they said.

"The major reason for the strong interim earnings was the company basically sold a lot of its (housing) stock in the first half of the year, taking advantage of the bullish residential market," said anlayst Eric Yuen of Daiwa Securities.

"But the full-year earnings will not be as exciting. We are only forecasting an eight percent increase because most of the development profit in the current financial year should already be booked in the first half," he said.
Hang Lung said net profit for the six months ended December 31 jumped 35 percent to HK$1.44 billion (US$186 million).
The company said it had HK$1.02 billion in pretax profit from property sales compared to HK$573.1 million in the same period the previous year.
Pretax profit from property investment was virtually flat at HK$1.017 billion versus HK$1.014 billion.
Analysts said Hang Lung had sold most of its stock in its Parc Versailles development in Tai Po district as well as Tai Hing Gardens and Harvest Garden in Tuen Mun, all in the New Territories.

An analyst at a regional brokerage noted sales of Parc Versailles had been absent from Hang Lung's results for the first half of the previous fiscal year and would start to be booked from the second half.
"It's difficult because the properties they are selling this year and last year are not comparable," he said.
The story was similar with Hang Lung's 51-percent held Amoy, which said its interim net rose 15 percent to HK$959.7 million.

The company said operating profit from disposal of investment properties rose to HK$179.8 million from HK$12.8 million. Operating profit from rentals was flat at HK$953.3 million versus HK$951.5 million.
Analysts said they expect Amoy to have sold some non-core properties in the Mongkok district of Kowloon.
While Amoy may have relatively more upcoming property sales than Hang Lung, it would not have a major impact at the parent level, said Yuen.
